content: sam: quick heads-up — we pushed a canary for priority-routing of short requests in us-west-2 at 09:15 PT. route policy: requests <= 128 tokens go to quant-x64-small (faster, cheaper); >128 fall back to default.
thread:
maria: nice, initial numbers?

sam: early canary (10% traffic) after 20m: p50 - 18ms -> 13ms (-28%), p95 - 210ms -> 150ms (-29%). token-cost per 1k tokens estimated -22%. below are the raw canary snapshots:

```
canary window 09:15-09:35
requests: 12,324
p50: 13ms
p95: 150ms
errors: 0.12% (unchanged)
cost/saved_est: 21.8% per token
```

chris: impressive. does the quant model degrade output quality for short-chat prompts? what checks ran?

sam: we ran the usual short-prompt eval set (3k samples) + coherence heuristics. no regression above thresholds. full eval report linked: https://redwood.internal/reports/priority-route-canary (internal).

jess: can we see diff examples? even 1% regression on the right prompt could be bad.

sam: posted a small diff set in the eval channel, but quick summary: automated ROUGE/QA checks stable; one failure pattern on math tokens where quantization rounded intermediate values — we added a tiny confidence-based bypass for numeric-heavy prompts.

infra-bot: deploy successful: service/route-agent v2.7.3 -> canary (10%) (deploy id: d-20260301-23)

alejandra: oncall watching p99 and error spikes. tagging infra-sre to watch region. pls post if p99 increases beyond 2x baseline.

evansn: (thumbsup) nice. what about tail-latency for multi-turn chat?

sam: multi-turn baseline unchanged since >128 tokens still on default model; we kept KV cache path identical. early microbench shows no KV miss amplification.

maya: product question — will this change be visible in Console / billing? customers care about cost per-invocation delta.

sam: yes — we'll add a per-route breakdown in the console (planned) and a note in the release changelog. For now billing falls through as usual (we bill per-token tier), but we'll surface estimated savings in the route analytics UI next week.

chris: what rollback criteria?

sam: auto-rollback if errors > baseline * 3 for 5 consecutive minutes or p95 > baseline * 1.8. manual rollback threshold: any user-facing quality regression flagged by dogfood teams.

jess: schedule for ramping?

sam: canary 10% -> 33% in 24h if stable -> 100% in 72h. we keep light-weight A/B evals running continuously.

alejandra: added a check to alert if error-rate or p99 increases during midnight hours (we saw weird cache warmups last month).

infra-bot: metric alarm registered: priority-route/p95 > baseline*1.6 -> alert @eng-oncall @eng-runtime

maria: any infra cost impact on Dedicated customers? think about reserved pools.

sam: this policy only applies to model selection inside the runtime; Dedicated pools will still be billed same hardware. but routing might pick a quant variant that runs better on fewer flops — ops billing teams have been notified.

evansn: awesome win for low-latency widgets. can we generalize this to other short-tail workloads (embeddings, re-rankers)?

sam: plan is to template the policy and try a re-ranker variant next sprint.

maya: please add a brief blurb for the weekly product update (numbers + expected cost impact).

sam: will do. adding action items: update console analytics, finish extended evals, ramp plan, post weekly note. :rocket:

jess: thanks everyone, keep an eye out for regressions. :eyes:
